Replace an id column with a readable column from the database

Source: R/add_column_from_db.R
add_column_from_db.Rd

Join a lookup table of the database to the data and replace an id column with the readable column of that table, for example trait_domain_id with trait_domain_name. Used by get_readable_column_names().

Usage

add_column_from_db(
  con = NULL,
  data_to_rename = NULL,
  sel_column_id = NA_character_,
  join_type = "left_join",
  sel_join_by = sel_column_id,
  sel_suffix = c("", ""),
  sel_column_name = NA_character_,
  table_name = NA_character_,
  sel_table = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

con

A valid DBI connection to the VegVault database, used to read table_name when sel_table is NULL.

data_to_rename

The data, a lazy table or a data frame.

sel_column_id

Character. The id column to replace.

join_type

Character. "left_join" keeps every row of the data; "inner_join" keeps only the rows with a match in the lookup table.

sel_join_by

The join columns, as for dplyr::left_join(). Defaults to sel_column_id.

sel_suffix

Character of length 2. The suffixes for columns that are in both the data and the lookup table, as for dplyr::left_join().

sel_column_name

Character. The readable column of the lookup table.

table_name

Character. The table of the database to join, when sel_table is NULL.

sel_table

A lazy table to join instead of table_name, or NULL.

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE (default) and the data already have sel_column_name, no table is joined: the existing column is kept and only the id column is removed.

Value

The data without sel_column_id, with sel_column_name in its place and the other columns of the lookup table added at the end.

Details

The data are returned unchanged when they do not have sel_column_id.

When the two suffixes are the same, a column of the lookup table that the data already have, other than the join columns, is not joined: the data keep their own. Without this, the join would create two columns of the same name. In VegVault 2.0.0, for example, the trait values carry trait_unit, and so does TraitsDomain.

See also

get_readable_column_names()
